events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.43 (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
The trip is RydeTAXI, metered: F7 shows a meter-structured fare (base, distance, time, waiting, platform) and F4 states the excess-distance figure as 4.80 km × $1.4100/km, "this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km" [F4][F7][RD-2]. So extra detour km feed directly into what the rider paid.

One off-route segment exists: 21:39–21:49, 6.27 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.71 km, adding 4.56 km [F3][RD-1]. It is not exempted by any traffic cause: F14 records no incidents near the route in the trip window, and F12/F13 are only category speed-band records on the expressway and Kampong Bahru Road, which under RD-4(b) are corroboration at most and do not exempt on their own [F12][F13][F14][RD-4][RD-1].

RD-3 does not rescue the segment either. RD-3(a) exempts a stop the rider named; here the rider did not name the petrol station — the driver proposed it ("the petrol station just ahead") and chose its location, and no stop was measured in the segment [F8][F9][F3][RD-3]. RD-3(b) is squarely on point: the rider consented to "stop for a moment", not to the driver's choice of where and by what route [F9][F11][RD-3][RD-5].

RD-5 fails as well. The only rider message before the segment is "Sure, no problem" at 21:36, answering the driver's request to pull in at a petrol station "just ahead" for one minute [F8][F9][F3]. Read in context that is a general assent to a brief stop, not a route authorisation: under RD-5(1) a general choice covers a route taken to get there, not the driver's own errand, and a stop away from the route or a loop that reaches nothing still counts. The driver's later statement that the rider "agreed to a short change of route" is a claim made after the trip, not rider consent, and cannot establish agreement (G11) [F11][F9][RD-5]. Moreover the driver never stopped for petrol at all, which is the rider's grievance and shows the driven loop served no agreed purpose [F9][F3][RD-5]. The segment therefore counts as a non-exempt detour, and it changes the amount.

Amount under RD-2: 4.56 km × $1.4100/km = $6.4296 → $6.43 [F3][F4][RD-2]. RD-6's flag condition fails (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0), so no account action [F17][RD-6]. NS-7: the refund is issued as a voucher, not cash, and Ryde retains final discretion [RD-2][NS-7].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the messages are a petrol-stop request and a one-word assent, and the complaint is about the route and the meter [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Nothing to escalate. Evidence: the record settles every element — 2 of 2 messages timestamped, the segment measured, the fare figures given [F3][F4][F7][F10].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.43 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the non-exempt 4.56 km detour, waive/deduct nothing else, and remind the driver that agreeing to a one-minute petrol stop does not authorise a 6.27 km loop.

Amount under RD-2: 4.56 km × $1.4100/km = $6.4296 → $6.43 [F3][F4][RD-2]. RD-6's flag condition fails (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0), so no account action [F17][RD-6]. NS-7: the refund is issued as a voucher, not cash, and Ryde retains final discretion [RD-2][NS-7].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the messages are a petrol-stop request and a one-word assent, and the complaint is about the route and the meter [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Nothing to escalate. Evidence: the record settles every element — 2 of 2 messages timestamped, the segment measured, the fare figures given [F3][F4][F7][F10].

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's position that the route change was covered by the rider's agreement rests only on his own post-trip statement, "the rider agreed to a short stop so I thought a small change of route was fine" [F11]; a claim of agreement appearing only in the driver's statement is not consent, and the rider's 21:36 message assented only to a one-minute petrol stop the driver proposed, not to a 4.56 km off-route loop [F8][F9][RD-5][RD-3].

The rider's request for no_action/acceptance of the stop cannot stand: the meter is RydeTAXI and the non-exempt segment's extra km enter the fare [F4][F7][RD-2]; the stop itself was never made (the complaint says he never stopped for petrol), so the segment is unexplained under RD-1 and not exempt under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [F3][F9][F14].

segment_findings.reason: Rider's only pre-segment message, "Sure, no problem" at 21:36, answers the driver's request to pull in at a petrol station "just ahead" for one minute [F8][F9]. That is assent to a brief stop, not a route authorisation: under RD-5(1) a general assent covers the route chosen to reach the destination, not a loop of the driver's own that reaches nothing, and the driver chose the location of the stop [RD-5]. RD-3(a) does not exempt because the rider named no place; RD-3(b) applies (rider did not name the location, the driver picked a point that produced an off-route segment); no stop was measured there. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider "agreed to a short change of route" is not consent [F11][RD-5][RD-3]. No traffic incident supports the diversion [F14][RD-4]. Segment counts, 4.56 km refundable under RD-2.

Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts.
